chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Durust, and Hisham ibn Salim, all from Ajlan Abi Salih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The one who drinks an intoxicant, or gives it to a child who does not have intellect, I will quench him with scalding water as a punishment or grant him forgiveness; and the one who leaves the intoxicant seeking My pleasure, I will admit him into Paradise, quench him from the sealed nectar, and deal with him in terms of prestige as I deal with My guardians.'

key_terms.الرَّحِيقِ الْمَخْتُومِ: The sealed nectar (a specific drink of Paradise)
key_terms.مَاءِ الْحَمِيمِ: Scalding water (a form of punishment in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for abstaining from intoxicants for the sake of God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this Hadith Qudsi emphasizes the spiritual merit of abstaining from intoxicants not merely as legal compliance but as an act of seeking divine pleasure (ibtigha' maradat Allah). It contrasts the punishment of drinking or feeding it to a child with the reward of Paradise and the 'Sealed Nectar' (Al-Raheeq Al-Makhoom) for the abstainer, highlighting the concept of divine intimacy with the righteous.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, and Dorost, and Hisham Bin Salim, altogether, from Ajlan Abu Salih who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: “The one who drinks an intoxicant, or quenches it to his young children not having the intellect, would be Quenched from the scalding water as a Punishment or there being Forgiveness for him; and the one who leaves the intoxicant seeking My<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure, I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Enter him into the Paradise, and Quench him from the sealed nectar, and would Deal with him from the prestige what I<sup>azwj</sup> would Deal with My Guardians<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Flafs ibn al-Bakhtariy and Durust and Flisham ibn Salim all from ‘Ajlan abu Salih who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “If one drinks an intoxicating liquor or makes a child, who does not understand, to drink it, I will make him to drink al-Hamim, regardless of whether he will suffer punishment or will be forgiven. One who quits intoxicating substances for My sake I will admit him in the garden (paradises) and give him sealed Rahiq (exquisite nectar in a sealed container) for a drink and will honor him as I will honor my friends.’”
